The 1-Tier PCM performed the best due to lower cycle costs, lower TES costs, and increased HTF capacity. The 1-Tier PCM resulted in a 25.5% decrease in ETES installed cost, a 9.8% decrease in LCOE, and a 74.3% increase in IRR. The salt-only 715°C case degraded the system metrics because the reduced HTF hot temperature reduces cycle efficiency, increases cycle cost, and decreases TES energy density. IRR was calculated using a constant power purchase agreement price; therefore, higher IRR values indicate that the system is more competitive and could be profitable at a lower agreement price. For all the HTF cases, the power cycle costs contribute to more than 40% of the ETES system’s total installed cost. With the addition of PCMs, the thermal energy storage portion of the installed cost decreases from approximately 17% to 12%. Figure 15 presents an sCO cycle capital cost breakdown for each component within the simple 2 configuration. In the salt-only and 3-Tier PCM HTF cases, the primary heat exchanger cost is the largest portion of the total sCO cycle cost. For the 2- and 1-Tier PCM cases, the compressor 2 cost becomes the largest portion of the total cycle cost.
